s1-workspace-gate.summaryMarkdown: Full re-review after the owner's epic amendment (`nsh-root` becomes a read-only reference, PR texts move to `gpuitizen:docs/pr/**`), which invalidated the stored review; the s1 criteria, tasks, checks and product source are unchanged since my reattested pass. Nothing in s1 depends on nsh-root: both tasks map only to `gpuitizen` paths, and no s1 file references `nsh-root`, `upstream-pr` or `docs/upstream`. README.md lists exactly the four execution repositories of the amended d01, and AGENTS.md keeps the no-NSH rule. WS-1/TGT-4: the workspace, pins, lints, release profile, toolchain, alias and licences comply, and `policy::tests` fails on each drift. TGT-1: both specs are correct (armv7 softfp with +v7,+thumb2,+vfp3,+neon, vendor tizen, 32-bit; x86_64 vendor tizen), and `targets::tests` checks the fields and that the pinned nightly accepts both. TGT-2: `cross::tests` covers the command lines and environment for both targets: build-std, the json spec, clang --target/--sysroot plus the armv7 flags, clang+lld linking via gcc-ld, the pinned RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, clippy with -D warnings, passthrough, --all-tv-libs, the early missing-rootstrap failure for linking builds only, inherited RUSTFLAGS merged into CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS, and --check-symbols rejected before Cargo. WS-2: AGENTS.md matches the workspace. Both earlier findings stay resolved. Risk to confirm at the first real link in s3: the x86_64 default rootstrap name `tizen-8.0-emulator64.core`.

s1b-gates.summaryMarkdown: TGT-3 and ARM64-1 hold as in the first review: Tizen-only `gpui-fast`/`gpui-fast-wgpu` `=0.1.13` under `cfg(target_vendor = "tizen")`, no desktop platform, font-kit, freetype or fontconfig-sys crates in any of the three Tizen graphs (`cargo tree`), the aarch64 spec checked by `targets::tests` and wired through `TIZEN_ROOTSTRAP_AARCH64`, gates passing. TGT-5 (amended) now matches the code: lookup, `ld.bfd`/`-B`/`-L` arguments matching the installed SDK layout, early failure, clang-only C, the linker choice keyed on toolchain presence with stable rustflags, accurate module docs and `docs/setup.md`, and `gcc::tests` (6 tests, run by the reviewer) covering arguments, lookup and failure for every target. All three earlier findings are resolved.

s2-bindings-host.summaryMarkdown: SYS-1 through HOST-2 hold at this snapshot. The bindings match the Tizen 8.0 headers and libraries, and the allowlist drift and forbidden-prefix tests fail on drift. `check-symbols` now counts every dynsym definition as an export, catching the IFUNC `i` and unique `u` cases. It also limits `DT_NEEDED` to glibc's five libraries, `libgcc_s`, the loader, and the declared Tizen libraries by exact soname, and all real rootstrap sonames pass. `package` stages exactly the library that was built and checked under cargo's `target_directory`, and feeds `dotnet build` that library and the rendered manifest. The four s2 findings are resolved (I reran symcheck::tests 8/8 and package::tests 6/6).

s3-diag.summaryMarkdown:
Full review at snapshot 8e193a62: all seven findings are resolved and verified in source.

- **wgpu errors**: error scopes wrap configure and every frame, and the uncaptured-error handler records errors instead of panicking. A panic hook writes to dlog.
- **EGL loading**: libEGL and libGLESv2 are held in process-lifetime `OnceLock` statics and never unloaded.
- **Partial reports**: the `complete` flag and the server waiting for the complete report work. `App::finish()` is used on every terminal path, including the cases where no window was created.
- **`diag pull`**: it runs `sdb forward`, with a `--no-forward` opt-out.
- **Server**: it binds loopback and sets a write timeout on each client.
- **`tizen-deps`**: it requires one wgpu in the workspace Tizen graph, which includes gpui-fast-wgpu, and requires the diag's wgpu to be that one.
- **Pause**: pause and resume delete and re-add the Ecore timer.

DIAG-1..4 are met. Reruns pass: report 8, probe 5, transport 9 and tizen_deps 5 tests, plus armv7 Clippy. The latest logs show both release links with `--check-symbols` (only `dxn_gpui_tizen_main` exported, no EGL or GLES linked) and both tizen-deps runs passing.

The behaviour on a real TV or the emulator is still unproven: this review is by reading only, and that check belongs to the owner-run device sprints.

findings.descriptionMarkdown: AGENTS.md and README.md documented the unavailable aarch64 target and a `--check-symbols` validation command that always failed after a full build. Resolved: the docs list only armv7/x86_64 and runnable validation commands, and `--check-symbols` now fails in `cross::plan` before Cargo runs.

Link args passed only via `CARGO_TARGET_<T>_RUSTFLAGS` were silently dropped when the caller set `RUSTFLAGS`/`CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`. Resolved: inherited flags are merged with the link args into one `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` and `RUSTFLAGS` is removed from the child environment.

**Expected (TGT-5):** "Non-linking builds keep the pinned toolchain's lld." **Observed:** `cross::plan` (`xtask/src/cross/mod.rs`, the `match &ctx.gcc_toolchain` block) chooses the linker by whether a GCC toolchain was *found*, not by whether the build links (`links = ctx.needs_link && !options.clippy`). On any machine with the SDK installed, the gate (`-p dxn_gpui_tizen`, an rlib build) and `--clippy` get `--ld-path=.../ld.bfd`/`-B`/`-L` instead of `-fuse-ld=lld -B<rustlib>/gcc-ld`; lld is used only when no toolchain exists. Harmless at run time (nothing is linked), and keying on presence keeps `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` identical between gate and linking builds (no full rebuild when switching), but the criterion text and the in-code comment on the `None` arm ("Non-linking builds (rlibs, clippy) never reach the linker; keep the pinned toolchain's lld") both state a condition the code does not implement, and no test exercises the lld branch at all (no `lld` assertion in `cross::tests`; `gcc::tests::missing_toolchain_fails_only_linking_builds` only checks `is_ok()`). **Repair:** pick one and make spec, comment and test agree: (a) preferred, amend TGT-5/`d34-gnu-ld-link` to "builds that do not link do not need the GCC toolchain; when none is found they keep the pinned toolchain's lld, otherwise they get the same GNU ld arguments as linking builds (stable rustflags)", reword the comment, and add an assertion in `gcc::tests` that `plan` with `ctx(None, false)` yields `-Clink-arg=-fuse-ld=lld` and `-Clink-arg=-B/tc/bin/gcc-ld` and no `--ld-path`; or (b) key the branch on `links` and add tests for both sides.

**Resolved:** TGT-5 and `d34-gnu-ld-link` now state the implemented rule (with the toolchain installed every build passes the GCC link arguments so rustflags match; without it only non-linking builds run, with lld standing in); the `None`-arm comment in `cross::plan` says the same; `gcc::tests::non_linking_builds_without_the_toolchain_use_lld` asserts `-fuse-ld=lld`, `-B/tc/bin/gcc-ld` and no `--ld-path` for `ctx(None, false)` and identical `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` for gate vs linking builds with the toolchain.

**Expected:** after TGT-5, the code documentation matches GNU-ld linking (the brief: "the docs match the code"). **Observed:** two module docs still describe the superseded TGT-2 lld link: `xtask/src/cross/mod.rs` lines 1-2 ("clang for C dependencies and clang + lld for linking against the Tizen rootstrap") and `xtask/src/gcc/mod.rs` lines 3-4 ("clang + lld find them through the `-B` / `-L` arguments built here"), contradicting `gcc::linker`, `gcc::link_args` and `docs/setup.md`, which say linking against the rootstrap uses `ld.bfd` because lld rejects it. `docs/setup.md`, `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` themselves are accurate. **Repair:** reword both module docs to "clang drives the link with the SDK's GNU `ld.bfd` (`--ld-path`), GCC's start files and `libgcc_s` (`gcc` module); lld only when no GCC toolchain is present for a non-linking build".

**Resolved:** Module docs of `xtask/src/cross/mod.rs` and `xtask/src/gcc/mod.rs` now say clang drives the SDK's GNU `ld.bfd` (`--ld-path`), with lld only for builds that never link on machines without the SDK toolchain.

**Expected (TGT-5):** "The `gcc::tests` group checks the arguments, lookup and failure for every target." **Observed (`xtask/src/gcc/tests.rs`):** arguments are asserted in full for armv7 and aarch64, but for x86_64 only `link_args(...)[3]` (`-L.../lib64`); its `--ld-path`, `-B` and GCC-lib `-L` are unchecked. `env()` is asserted only for armv7, so `TIZEN_GCC_TOOLCHAIN_X86_64` / `TIZEN_GCC_TOOLCHAIN_AARCH64` (the names `docs/setup.md` and `README.md` document) are asserted nowhere; the failure path (`missing_toolchain_fails_only_linking_builds`) and `gcc::missing` are exercised only for armv7, so the x86_64/aarch64 error text (directory `x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc-9.2` / `aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc-9.2`, env name, `NativeToolchain-Gcc-9.2`) is untested. Lookup is covered once per target (env/SDK/home split across targets), which is acceptable. **Repair:** replace the per-target spot checks with a loop over `Target::ALL` and an expected table `(target, env name, sdk dir, gcc triple, runtime lib dir)` asserting the full four-element `link_args`, `env(target)`, `candidates(target, None, Some("/sdk"), None) == [/sdk/tools/<dir>]`, and that `plan` with a linking `ctx(None, true)` for that target fails with an error naming the dir, the env variable and `NativeToolchain-Gcc-9.2`.

**Resolved:** `gcc::tests::every_target_has_link_args_lookup_and_failure` iterates a table sized to `Target::ALL` and asserts, per target, the full four-element `link_args` (ld.bfd, `-B`, GCC-lib `-L`, `lib`/`lib64`), `env()`, the SDK candidate `/sdk/tools/<dir>`, and that `missing()` names the dir, env variable, `NativeToolchain-Gcc-9.2` and the searched path; the armv7 `plan` failure path stays covered by `missing_toolchain_fails_only_linking_builds`.

**Expected (SYS-3, d07):** `check-symbols` fails unless the library exports exactly one global symbol. **Observed:** `symcheck::check` (`xtask/src/symcheck/mod.rs`) counts as exports only defined symbols whose nm letter is uppercase (`filter(|s| s.kind.is_ascii_uppercase())`). The pinned toolchain's `llvm-nm` prints global exports in lowercase for two ELF kinds: STT_GNU_IFUNC as `i` and STB_GNU_UNIQUE as `u`. Verified by linking a probe with the pinned `rust-lld -shared`: `llvm-nm -D --defined-only` printed `00000000000012f4 i my_ifunc` and `0000000000003368 u uniq` next to `D entry`. Both are real `.dynsym` exports, and the checker would let them pass without a word. So the one-export gate can give false negatives. **Repair:** treat every line of `llvm-nm -D --defined-only` as an export (lld writes no local symbols into `.dynsym`), and keep `W`/`V` as the weak ones. Add `symcheck::tests` fixtures with an `i` line and a `u` line that must report `ExtraExport`.

**Expected (SYS-3):** imports come only from `symbols.allow` plus glibc's `libc`, `libm`, `libdl`, `libpthread`, `librt`, `ld-linux`, plus `libgcc_s` and the loader. **Observed:** the checker accepts any undefined symbol whose version starts with `GLIBC_` or `GCC_` (`SYSTEM_VERSION_PREFIXES`). It never looks at which library provides the symbol. Imports from other glibc libraries therefore pass: for example `res_query@GLIBC_2.4` from `libresolv`, `forkpty@GLIBC_2.4` from `libutil`, `getaddrinfo_a` from `libanl`, `libnsl`, `libcrypt`, or `libmvec` on x86_64. None of these is in the criterion's list. **Repair:** also read `DT_NEEDED` with the pinned `llvm-readobj --needed-libs` (it ships next to `llvm-nm` in rustlib/bin). Require every needed entry to be `libc.so.6`, `libm.so.6`, `libdl.so.2`, `libpthread.so.0`, `librt.so.1`, an `ld-linux*.so.*`, `libgcc_s.so.1`, or `lib<name>.so*` for a library recorded in `DECLARED_SYMBOLS`. Report each other entry by name, and add a fixture test with an extra `libresolv.so.2`.

**Expected (HOST-2):** `package` stages the library that `cargo xtask cross` just built and symbol-checked. **Observed:** `run_cross` finds built libraries under `cargo metadata`'s `target_directory`. `run_package` (`xtask/src/main.rs`) then copies from `cross::built_libraries(&root.join("target"), ...)`. When `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` or `build.target-dir` is set, the two paths differ: `package` copies a stale, unchecked `target/<spec>/release/lib<app>.so` if one exists, and fails at the copy otherwise. **Repair:** have `run_cross` return, or let `run_package` look up, the libraries under the metadata `target_directory`. Stage exactly the paths that went through `check_symbols`.

**Expected (HOST-1, d08):** the csproj includes the staged library through `TizenTpkUserIncludeFiles`, and that inclusion is part of how TPKs are built. **Observed:** the `TizenTpkUserIncludeFiles` item only applies when `$(DxnAppLibrary)` is set. Its comment says ``passed by `cargo xtask package` (`-p:DxnAppLibrary=...`)``, but `run_package` runs `dotnet build -c Release <csproj>` without that property. The SDK path is also off (`TizenCreateTpkOnBuild=false`), so the item is never used. `TizenManifestFile` points at `tizen-manifest.template.xml`, which still has its `{{...}}` placeholders, so any SDK-built TPK would ship an unrendered manifest. **Repair:** pick one: (a) pass `-p:DxnAppLibrary=<the checked library>` from `run_package`, and point `TizenManifestFile` at the rendered manifest for SDK builds; or (b) correct the comment to say the item serves only an SDK-built TPK and that `cargo xtask package` stages `lib/libdxn_app.so` itself, and make sure the template is never used as an SDK manifest.

**Expected** (DIAG-2, t3-probe): a failed stage is recorded with its name and error text; the probe never panics and a failure never stops the report from being served.

**Observed** `src/tizen/wgpu_backend.rs` installs no uncaptured-error handler and no error scope. In wgpu 30.0.1, `Surface::configure` sends its error to the device's error sink (`backend/wgpu_core.rs:3975-3981`), and the default handler is `panic!("wgpu error: ...")` (`backend/wgpu_core.rs:692-695`). `queue.submit` and `begin_render_pass` validation errors take the same path. With `panic = "abort"`, a configure failure on the TV's EGL (an unsupported format or extent, exactly the #10708 class of failure) aborts the process: the report server thread dies with it, nothing is served, and the panic text goes only to stderr. `configure()` returns `Ok` without checking whether configuration succeeded.

**Repair**: after `request_device`, call `device.on_uncaptured_error(...)` with a handler that only records the error (an `Arc<Mutex<Option<String>>>` the backend reads) and never panics. Wrap `surface.configure` and each frame's encode/submit/present in `device.push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation)` and `pollster::block_on(scope.pop())`, and turn `Some(err)` into the stage's `Err(..)`. Also install a `std::panic::set_hook` in `dxn_gpui_tizen_main` that sends the panic message to dlog (tag `DXN_DIAG`), so a wgpu-hal internal panic (for example the `unwrap`s in `wgpu-hal/src/gles/egl.rs`) at least leaves a trace before the abort. Optionally, also write the last report and the panic to the app's data directory, so the next launch can serve them.

**Expected** (DIAG-1, `egl.rs` module doc): EGL and GL ES are loaded at run time, and the display is left initialized for wgpu.

**Observed** in `src/tizen/egl.rs`: `query()` owns the `libEGL` `Library` in a local, so it is `dlclose`d when `query` returns. `read_gles()` drops `libGLESv2` before `gles_query` releases the still-current context. Nothing else in the process links libEGL (the cdylib's NEEDED list has no EGL or GLES), so the reference count can reach zero and glibc can unmap the GPU driver. That happens while the `EGLDisplay` is still initialized (no `eglTerminate`) and while any threads or atexit handlers the driver created are still live. The result is undefined behaviour, a likely crash on Mali drivers, and the doc's claim that the display is "left initialized for wgpu" does not hold.

**Repair**: keep both libraries loaded for the life of the process. Either store them in a `static OnceLock<Library>` or in `App`, or open them with `libloading::os::unix::Library::open(Some(name), RTLD_NOW | RTLD_NODELETE)`. Release the context (`eglMakeCurrent(NO_*)`) before the GL library handle can go away.

**Expected**: a client receives the complete report once it exists. A partial report is served only after a timeout, marked incomplete. Every terminal path, including the cases where no window was created, marks the report complete.

**Resolution**:
- `Report.complete` exists, and `Shared::wait` waits for a complete report, falling back to the latest partial one on timeout.
- `summary()` prints `running (partial report ...)` for an incomplete report.
- `App::finish()` sets `complete` and `finished`, clears the timer handle and publishes. It is used by both window-failure branches of `create` and both terminal paths of `tick`.
- The only plain `publish()` left is the partial report published after the collectors run.
- Covered by the tests `a_partial_report_waits_for_the_complete_one` and `a_timeout_serves_the_latest_partial_report_marked_running`.

**Expected** (DIAG-3, and the help text "fetch the diagnostic app's report through `sdb forward`"): `cargo xtask diag pull [--port

]` connects through `sdb forward tcp:

tcp:

`. **Observed**: `run_diag` (`xtask/src/main.rs`) only connects to `127.0.0.1:`. It never sets up the forward, and only mentions it in the error context. **Repair**: before connecting, run `sdb forward tcp:

tcp:

`. Find `sdb` on `PATH` or under `$TIZEN_SDK`/`~/tizen-studio/tools/sdb`, and report a clear error if `sdb` or a device is missing. Keep an opt-out such as `--no-forward` for a tunnel the user sets up by hand. Put the argument and path resolution in a testable helper with a unit test.

**Expected**: the report is reached from the Mac through `sdb forward`, which connects to the device's loopback interface.

**Observed**: `transport::start` binds `0.0.0.0:<port>` (`src/transport/mod.rs:96-102`). Anyone on the TV's LAN can read the device model, the driver strings and the logs. Accepted streams also have no write timeout, so a peer that connects and never reads can block the single-client server.

**Repair**: bind `127.0.0.1`, unless LAN access is an intended use, in which case document it as a design decision. Call `set_write_timeout` on each accepted stream, for example 10 s.

**Expected** (DIAG-4, d09): `tizen-deps` shows that the diag graph holds one wgpu, *the version gpui-fast-wgpu uses*, so that the workspace lock holds one wgpu.

**Observed**: `xtask/src/tizen_deps/mod.rs` compares the diag graph against the constant `WGPU_MAJOR = 30`. Suppose the gpui-fast pin moves to a release built on wgpu 31 and the constant is not updated. The workspace Tizen graph would then hold two wgpu, while the diag graph still holds exactly one 30.x, and the check would still print the OK line. The lock holds one wgpu today, so the criterion is met at this snapshot.

**Repair**: compute the expected version from the workspace Tizen graph instead of hard-coding it. Either take the wgpu that `gpui-fast-wgpu` resolves to (`cargo tree -p gpui-fast-wgpu` or `-i wgpu`), or require that the workspace graph (`tree(None)`) holds exactly one `wgpu` and that the diag's wgpu is that one. Add a test for a workspace graph with two wgpu versions.

**Expected** (constraint: the main thread stays responsive; d11: Fifo paced by Ecore_Wl2 frame callbacks): no Ecore callback blocks for long.

**Observed**: `pause` and `resume` only log (`src/tizen/mod.rs:336-344`). If the app is sent to the background during the 120-frame probe, the 0.0 s Ecore timer keeps calling `present`. With Fifo, the Wayland EGL swap may wait indefinitely for a frame callback that a hidden surface never receives. That would block the main loop until the watchdog kills the app.

**Repair**: record `paused` in `App`. While paused, `tick` skips probe steps (it returns RENEW without presenting, or the timer is frozen with `ecore_timer_freeze` and thawed on `resume`). Log the pause in the report, and have the probe report state that the probe was interrupted if it never resumes.

Resolved. `--verify` seeds `release::SCRATCH_LOCK` (`artifacts-temp/locks/gpui-fast-patch/Cargo.lock`, ignored) from `Cargo.lock` and passes `resolver.lockfile-path` through `cross::lockfile_config`; `run_gpui_fast_release` compares `Cargo.lock`'s bytes before/after the patched `cargo tree`, restores and fails on a difference. `cargo xtask cross` routes any build whose cargo args carry `--config …gpui-fast-patch.toml` to the same scratch lock (`release::uses_patch_config`, test `patched_builds_are_recognized`); its own unpatched `cargo_metadata` call stays on the committed lock. Verified: the scratch lock holds the patched resolution (path-sourced `gpui-fast`/`-macros`/`-wgpu`, six desktop `[[patch.unused]]`), the root `Cargo.lock` equals HEAD after the re-executed verify and after my scoped xtask test run. Rule recorded in `d35-tizen-lints-scratch-lock`.

Resolved. The unchecked second `cargo tree --workspace` is gone. `release::verify_lock` parses the patched lockfile (every target, not only armv7): it fails when the lock does not parse or holds no packages, when a `[[patch.unused]]` name is also a `[[package]]` name (that sibling came from crates.io), and when `gpui-fast` is absent or still has a `source`; `verify_tree` keeps the `-i gpui-fast` root-path check, and a failed `cargo tree` bails. An unreadable scratch lock becomes an empty string and fails as "no packages". Covered by `the_patched_lock_passes_with_only_desktop_patches_unused`, `an_unused_patch_of_a_crate_the_graph_holds_fails`, `gpui_fast_from_the_registry_or_an_empty_graph_fails`.

Resolved by amendment. GF-4 now names `wgpu-test-lints` (cut from upstream `main`, cherry-picked into `tizen`); d06's invariants say each change branch passes library-target clippy on its own and the `--all-targets` clippy runs on `tizen`; the new decision `d35-tizen-lints-scratch-lock` records the fourth branch. Verified against git: `wgpu-test-lints` is one commit on fb8cf94 touching only `src/fast/`, and `tizen` = cd20d12 + the four branches' commits.

Resolved. `copy_tree` skips `release::NOT_RELEASED` (`target`, `Cargo.lock`, `.git`; test `the_release_branch_keeps_only_generated_files`). `tizen-release` is now 4305248 (parent b01dbc8, generated from `tizen` at 8e8825327589): its 478 files equal `target/release-workspace` minus `target/` and the cargo-written `Cargo.lock`, and no `Cargo.lock` or `target` path is in the tree. The release workspace has no nested entry with those names, so the recursive skip removes nothing prepare-release wrote.

Resolved. `pipeline_cache::open` now clears `CURRENT` before deciding whether the new device gets a cache (commit 5fa71b0 on `pipeline-cache`, still unstacked on fb8cf94; cherry-picked to `tizen` as 8e88253, file identical on both). A rejected adapter's device is no longer kept alive by the slot, matching the module comment. No GPU test was added for the slot (it needs a device); the optional temporary cache directory for GPU tests was not taken, which I accept as non-blocking.
